text:
### Real Examples  
**Case 1: Danske Bank (AML Failure)**
- Issue: Allowed £200B suspicious money through
- Consequence: €1B fine, CEO resigned, reputation destroyed
- Why: Staff ignored suspicious transactions  
**Case 2: Wells Fargo (Account Fraud)**
- Issue: Staff created fake accounts without authorization
- Consequence: $3B fine, CEO prosecution, massive layoffs
- Why: Pressure to meet targets; ignored ethics  
**Case 3: Facebook (GDPR Violation)**
- Issue: Shared user data without consent
- Consequence: €110M fine, ongoing investigation
- Why: Didn't respect user data rights
name: Chunk 54/61

raw_entities.name: Large Cash Deposit Followed by Immediate Transfer Out
raw_entities.description: A suspicious transaction pattern where substantial cash is deposited and then immediately transferred out of an account, indicative of money laundering layering techniques. This red flag is exemplified by the Danske Bank case where £200B in suspicious money was allowed to flow through the system.
context: Danske Bank (AML Failure) - Issue: Allowed £200B suspicious money through
Why: Staff ignored suspicious transactions

raw_entities.name: Unauthorized Account Creation Without Customer Consent
raw_entities.description: Staff creating accounts in customer names without proper authorization or customer knowledge. This misconduct signal was central to the Wells Fargo scandal where employees systematically opened unauthorized accounts to meet sales targets.
context: Wells Fargo (Account Fraud) - Issue: Staff created fake accounts without authorization
Why: Pressure to meet targets; ignored ethics

raw_entities.name: Unauthorized Data Sharing Without Customer Consent
raw_entities.description: Sharing or transferring customer personal data to third parties without explicit customer consent or authorization. This data protection red flag resulted in the Facebook GDPR violation where user data was shared without proper consent mechanisms.
context: Facebook (GDPR Violation) - Issue: Shared user data without consent
Why: Didn't respect user data rights

raw_entities.name: Obligation to Report Suspicious Transactions
raw_entities.description: Staff must identify and report suspicious transactions to compliance authorities. Failure to fulfill this obligation, as demonstrated in the Danske Bank case, results in severe regulatory penalties and reputational damage.
context: Danske Bank (AML Failure) - Why: Staff ignored suspicious transactions
Consequence: €1B fine, CEO resigned, reputation destroyed

raw_entities.name: Obligation to Obtain Customer Authorization for Account Operations
raw_entities.description: Staff must obtain explicit customer authorization before opening accounts or conducting transactions on behalf of customers. Violation of this obligation, as seen in Wells Fargo, constitutes fraud and results in significant fines and criminal prosecution.
context: Wells Fargo (Account Fraud) - Issue: Staff created fake accounts without authorization
Consequence: $3B fine, CEO prosecution, massive layoffs

raw_entities.name: Obligation to Respect User Data Rights and Obtain Consent
raw_entities.description: Organizations must respect customer data rights and obtain explicit consent before sharing or processing personal data. Failure to comply with this obligation, as demonstrated by Facebook's GDPR violation, results in substantial fines and ongoing regulatory investigation.
context: Facebook (GDPR Violation) - Issue: Shared user data without consent
Consequence: €110M fine, ongoing investigation

raw_entities.name: Wells Fargo Unauthorized Account Creation Event
raw_entities.description: A major fraud event where Wells Fargo staff systematically created unauthorized accounts without customer knowledge or consent to meet sales targets. This resulted in $3B in fines, CEO prosecution, and massive organizational layoffs.
context: Wells Fargo (Account Fraud) - Issue: Staff created fake accounts without authorization
Consequence: $3B fine, CEO prosecution, massive layoffs
